opening.argument: The presentation is framed as an institutional security discussion, with a conference slide identifying “Self-Custody Infrastructure for Institutions” alongside Anchorage Digital and the speaker’s description of a “regulated crypto platform” serving institutional clients. Its references to Porto and vaults explain infrastructure, including encryption, access controls, and authentication, rather than directing viewers to send funds or disclose credentials. The discussion of altered transaction data and supply-chain risks is presented as a cautionary example, followed by operational guidance that the signer should review transactions in a human-readable format on the signing device. The closing reminder to keep keys and transactions safe reinforces that the material is educational and focused on risk mitigation, including the cited Bybit loss, not an acquisition or payment request.

citations.quote: We are a regulated crypto platform and purpose-built to serve the unique needs of institutional clients in the digital asset space.

With crypto transactions, unfortunately when what you see on your screen isn't always what you're actually signing and malicious intermediaries and the supply chain can settle subtly alter the transaction data without you even knowing.

the person signing the transaction is the first line of defense and if the transactions are presented in a human readable auditable format directly on the signing device this will eliminate any of the guesswork involved
